blocks.raw: # Configure SFTP server for data export
blocks.text: Configure SFTP server for data export

blocks.raw: Brands are required to have their own Secure FTP (SFTP) infrastructure for exporting data. Currently, Capillary supports data exports only via SFTP.
blocks.text: Brands are required to have their own Secure FTP (SFTP) infrastructure for exporting data. Currently, Capillary supports data exports only via SFTP.

blocks.raw: You can configure up to five SFTP servers. After the data is exported to the SFTP server, you can download it to your local machine.
blocks.text: You can configure up to five SFTP servers. After the data is exported to the SFTP server, you can download it to your local machine.

blocks.raw:
> 📘 Note
>
> An SFTP once added you cannot be deleted or renamed. However, you can change server details and the path within that SFTP.
blocks.text: NoteAn SFTP once added you cannot be deleted or renamed. However, you can change server details and the path within that SFTP.

blocks.raw: # Setting up the public key in the Capillary SFTP server
blocks.text: Setting up the public key in the Capillary SFTP server

blocks.raw: Upload your SSH public key to the Capillary SFTP server before using SSH-based authentication. The SFTP server uses the public key to validate your connection when files are transferred.
blocks.text: Upload your SSH public key to the Capillary SFTP server before using SSH-based authentication. The SFTP server uses the public key to validate your connection when files are transferred.

blocks.raw: ## Prerequisites
blocks.text: Prerequisites

blocks.raw:
* Access to the Capillary SFTP server
* Permission to create folders
blocks.text: Access to the Capillary SFTP serverPermission to create folders

blocks.raw: ## Set up the public key
blocks.text: Set up the public key

blocks.raw: To set up the public key,
blocks.text: To set up the public key,

blocks.raw:
1. Sign in to the Capillary SFTP portal at using your username and password. The SFTP home page appears. 2. Select the **Profile** icon and select **My account**.
The **My Account** page opens. 3. Select **Authentication > SFTP/SSH Keys**. 4. Click **New SFTP/SSH Key**.
The **Create SFTP/SSH Key** page opens. 5. Under **Title**, enter a name for the SSH key. 6. Under **Key pair**, choose one of the following options:
- [Use your own](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/configure-ftp-server-for-data-export#ssh-authentication)
- Generate in browser For details on creating the key using the different options, refer 7. Under **Public key**, paste your SSH public key. 8. Select **Save**.

blocks.raw: ## SSH authentication
blocks.text: SSH authentication

blocks.raw: SSH (Secure Shell Protocol) is a secure method of connecting to your SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) servers for data transfer. Instead of passwords, SSH authentication relies on a key pair: a public key and a private key.
blocks.text: SSH (Secure Shell Protocol) is a secure method of connecting to your SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) servers for data transfer. Instead of passwords, SSH authentication relies on a key pair: a public key and a private key.

blocks.raw:
* **Private key**: Stored on your device and used when you connect to the server.
* **Public key**: Shared with the access team, who link it to your username on the SFTP server to enable SSH-based authentication.
blocks.text: Private key: Stored on your device and used when you connect to the server.Public key: Shared with the access team, who link it to your username on the SFTP server to enable SSH-based authentication.

blocks.raw: Optionally, you can add a passphrase when creating your key for additional security.
blocks.text: Optionally, you can add a passphrase when creating your key for additional security.

blocks.raw: ### Steps to create SSH authentication for SFTP
blocks.text: Steps to create SSH authentication for SFTP

blocks.raw: To use SSH for SFTP connections, complete the following steps to generate the SSH key pair:
blocks.text: To use SSH for SFTP connections, complete the following steps to generate the SSH key pair:

blocks.raw:
1. Open your terminal (macOS or Windows) and run the command: ```text Bash ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -m PEM -C "tom.sawyer@capillarytech.com" ``` **Note**: Only PEM file formats are supported to store the keys.

The command uses the following options: * `-t`: Specifies the key algorithm. RSA is recommended. * `-b`: Specifies the key length in bits. A higher value indicates stronger encryption. * `-m`: Saves the private key in PEM format. * `-C`: Adds a comment, typically your email address, for identification. 2. When prompted, choose a location to save the keys. The default locations are: * macOS: `/Users/user_name/.ssh/` * Windows: `C:\Users\user_name\.ssh\` Two files are generated: * `id_rsa`: Private key. The private key is in OpenSSH format, including the header and footer lines (`-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----` and `-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----`). * `id_rsa.pub`: Public key. 3. Optional: When prompted, add a passphrase to secure the key. Select **Enter** to skip if you do not want a passphrase.
